Wattwheels Bene V1.5 Electric Bike E-Bike 300W Belt Drive Commuter E-Bike Electric Bike Hydraulic Brakes Premium Smart Bike Trail Wattwheels WorkRide Eligible The top of the Wattwheels range, and it earns the position. The Bene is what you buy when you have looked at the rest of the line-up and decided you would rather not compromise. Sleek European styling, a drivetrain that asks almost nothing of you, and a component list that reads like a bike costing considerably more. Why we feature it The headline is the drivetrain. A Gates CDX carbon belt paired with an Enviolo Trekking internal gear hub means no chain, no derailleur, no gear cables, and no oiling. You change gear by twisting the grip — smoothly, through an infinite range, and at a standstill if you want to. Pull up at the lights in the wrong gear and it simply does not matter. For a bike that will do thousands of commuting kilometres, that is the difference between regular workshop visits and almost none. Power is the Ananda M100 mid-drive at 300W with 120N·m of torque, fed by a 720Wh Samsung pack. It is quiet, it responds to how hard you are pedalling rather than lurching, and the range is generous enough that most riders stop thinking about charging. The comfort kit is where the Bene pulls away from the Bighorn. A Suntour X1 Boost air fork with lockout is genuinely adjustable to your weight and riding style rather than a one-size coil. The KS Rage suspension dropper post does two jobs at once — drops the saddle out of the way at a stop, and takes the sting out of rough surfaces while you ride. Tektro Gemini four-piston hydraulic brakes are serious stopping hardware. Maxxis Rekon Race tyres in 2.4″ handle gravel and trail without feeling slow on tarmac, which suits the way most people actually use these bikes — sealed roads during the week, something rougher at the weekend. Smart connectivity A 4G SIM module is built in, paired to the Wattwheels app: real-time GPS location, geo-fencing alerts if the bike moves without you, remote lighting and assistance control, remote diagnostics, and the ability to report it stolen — which shuts the bike down. The app subscription is included for the first year and renews at $59.95 per year after that. It is entirely optional — the bike rides normally without it. Tracking functions require 4G coverage, and we recommend removing the battery if the bike will sit unused for more than a week or two. WorkRide eligible At 300W the Bene V1.5 sits inside the WorkRide power limit, so it can be purchased through the scheme if your employer is signed up. Talk to us about how that works. The Bighorn S is the step-over version of our best-selling all-rounder — identical running gear, different frame. If you are taller, ride harder, or simply grew up on a traditional diamond frame, this is the Bighorn for you. Why we feature it The top tube frame is stiffer than the low step, which you notice when you are putting power down or carrying weight on the rack. It also sits you in a slightly more forward, purposeful riding position — less upright cruiser, more capable hybrid. Riders coming off a road or mountain bike tend to feel at home on it immediately. Underneath, it is the same proven package. The Ananda M100 mid-drive delivers 300W and 120N·m of torque, which is what gets you up a steep pinch without dropping to walking pace. The 720Wh battery uses Samsung 21700 cells and is large enough that range stops being something you plan around — one of our customers took a Bighorn 700km through the Southland and Otago trails and was still seeing 80km of real-world range per charge. The S gets a Shimano Deore 10-speed Linkglide drivetrain, a step up from the Cues groupset on the low step model. Linkglide is engineered specifically for the torque an e-bike puts through a chain, so it holds up where a standard drivetrain wears out. Tektro hydraulic discs on 180mm rotors handle the stopping, and a Suntour XCM34 fork with lockout takes the buzz out of gravel. Everything you need is fitted from new: mudguards, rear rack, front and rear lights, and a colour display with a USB port. Which Bighorn should you buy? Mechanically the LS and the S are near-identical, so it comes down to the frame. Choose the LS if you want the easiest possible mount and dismount, ride in work clothes, or have any hip or mobility considerations. Choose the S if you are taller, want the stiffer frame, or just prefer the look of a crossbar. Both come in at the same price.
